text:
maria: Quick heads-up — after the host update on gpu-23 (driver 545.12) some long-seq traffic started getting routed to the slow fp32 kernel path instead of the sm-optimized fp8 path. p95 generation latency +12%.
aj: ugh. was that the auto-probe rollout? which heuristic flipped?
maria: looks like our capability bit extractor misread the tensorcore_fp8 flag. probe logs show hw_caps=(SM:sm92, tc:1, bf16:1, fp8:0) but nvidia-smi reports fp8 supported.
devon: can you paste the probe dump? also which sequence lengths are hitting it?
maria: here —
```
# probe dump from gpu-23
hw_sig: 0x7c3a
sm: "sm92"
reported_caps: {tensorcore: true, bf16: true, fp8_reported: false}
driver: "545.12"
kernel_pool: [fp8_fast, bf16_fast, fp32_ref]
selected_kernel_hint: "fp32_ref"
```
sequences: mostly 256-1024 tokens; traffic spike around 512.
sandra: note: routing heuristic has a seq-length hysteresis at 384. if fp8 path is gated by both driver flag and sm-feature match, a missing fp8 bit will push 512->fp32.
aj: could be a driver regression where FP8 is exposed via new query enum. our extractor expects the old enum.
ken: I saw something similar on gpu-11 last month with driver 538->543 where tc support was readable only via `nvmlDeviceGetCudaComputeCapability` variant.
devon: can we repro locally with an image pinned to 545.12? also capture perf counters to confirm kernel selection cost.
maria: repro steps I ran:
```
docker run --rm --gpus all redwood/infer-runtime:canary-2026-03 
./probe --dump /tmp/probe.json
./bench --model:gpt-small --seq 512 --batch 4 --steps 50 --trace perf_counter > perf.log
```
perf.log snippet:
```
step,lat_ms,tokens
1,112.3,128
10,118.7,512
25,124.5,512
50,130.9,512  # p95 drift upward
```
aj: those latencies look close to fp32_ref numbers. do we have kernel-level timings?
maria: yes — kernel profiler shows heavy time in matmul_sgemm kernel. fp8_fast never launched due to capability check failing at init.
ops-bot: deployment event: gpu-23 host-update 545.12 rolled out to pool-a at 2026-03-15T09:18:44Z.
sandra: action item: add a fallback probe that queries both old and new enums + a small runtime feature probe that attempts a minimal fp8 matmul microkernel at startup (non-fatal) to verify true support.
ken: +1 for microkernel probe. would catch mismatches where driver reports different flags. also add a seq threshold debug metric so we can spot when 384->512 crosses to fp32.
devon: I'll open a small PR: probe:dual-enum + microkernel-touch and a canary rollout to pool-b only. will include telemetry: kernel_selected, seq_len_bin, driver_version.
aj: also consider adding a short-circuit: if p95 increases by >8% over baseline for seq_bin[512], force re-eval of kernel picks and try soft-fallback to quantized BF16 path while we validate fp8.
maria: agreed. for the incident right now I've temporarily pinned gpu-23 workloads to dedicated-pool with older driver images.
ken: let's also add a visible alert rule in console: if kernel_selected == fp32_ref for any sm>=sm90 and driver_version >= 540, create a low-priority alert (ops) so we're not blind.
sandra: note for postmortem: record exact probe output, driver version matrix, and the microkernel attempt logs. include candidate repro scripts.
maria: I'll collect logs and open the incident ticket with repro steps + attach perf traces. thanks all. :thumbsup:
